cells.tense: You are standing where a change has settled and the form around it is holding steady.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Pick one piece you share with another person — a meal, a story, a way of marking a season — and let this exchange run both directions. What you hand over, something comes back of the same weight. Watch where it lands between you, and stop there.
cells.core:
You're standing where something changed and settled, and what you keep is holding. The practices, the words, the way your people do things — they came out of something real, and they're steady now because you've kept them steady. This is the part of a life where the shared thing has taken its shape and can be handed on, and it holds because nobody carries it alone.

The next move is small. Pick one piece you share with another person — a meal you cook together, a story you both tell, a way you mark a season — and let this exchange run both ways. What you give, something comes back of the same weight. Watch where it lands. What you keep will sit lighter after, and you'll see which people are actually carrying it with you rather than watching from the side.
cells.sheetLine: What you keep holds because no one carries it alone.

cells.place: in the shared meaning and tradition a person keeps and hands forward

cells.tense: You will make sure the shared thing survives, gripping it so hard nothing can touch the shape.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Go once toward whatever pulls at you and find out what it actually is. Not to replace anything you keep — just to see it up close. Stay as long as it holds your attention; nothing more is asked of you.
cells.core:
You are protecting something that was hard-won, and the protecting has gotten ahead of you. Every practice, every word you pass on is being defended before anything threatens it — the shape stays, but the people it was made for feel your grip on it. What was supposed to be shared is being kept safe from the ones it was meant for, and whatever else might still be possible with it gets read as a danger.

Try it the other way. Let something you keep sit where it is, and go once toward whatever draws you — not to swap it out, just to find out what it is. You don't have to choose it. What you left will still be there when you look back. What comes first is usually the plain pleasure of being pulled toward something instead of bracing against it.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding the form from the people it was for.

cells.tense: The shared thing kept going without you, and you have been standing outside the door.
cells.act: refuse the pull off course, once more
cells.ask: Refuse the next pull that tries to take you off something you know matters. Stay where you are and don't move. Nothing follows the refusal — no plan, no next step. The standing is the whole act.
cells.core:
The practices and meanings around you are still there, and you are not in them. You hold what you have by not showing up — not adding a word, not putting a hand in, not saying what you actually think — and the things you would once have carried forward are being held at a distance. The people near it can feel the absence, and so can you. Something you care about is waiting for you to decide again, and you have not decided anything in a while.

Start from feeling, not duty. Take something you know matters — a phrase, a meal, a way of doing things — and when the next pull tries to take you off it, refuse. Stand there once. This is not taking over; it is staying where you already are. The direction comes back in pieces, and the first piece is the one you did not hand away.
cells.sheetLine: You keep what you have by staying outside it.

cells.tense: You are already keeping something steady, and the keeping has been written off as the place's own nature.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Set it back when something shared starts to drift — a word in the right place, no explanation, nothing announced. Then, later, notice that the hand was yours. That noticing is the only thing to carry.
cells.core:
Something is holding, and you have been treating that as ordinary. Someone brings up the practice again, someone looks around for what to do, and the thing is steady before anyone sees who steadied it. You are the one. The structure you keep for your people is being filed under how things naturally work, and the ones who benefit from it mostly don't see it either.

Go back to the plain act. Next time something you share begins to drift, put it back without announcing it, and notice afterward that it was you. Deciding it and doing it in the same moment puts your name back on the thing you've been carrying quietly. Once is enough; seeing it is the part that was missing.
cells.sheetLine: The way things hold here runs through your hands.
